title: Runtime scheduler instrumentation: enqueue/dequeue tracing, per-class queue depth, wait-time histograms
author: Julian Moore
body:
Context: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype needs first-class visibility into queueing behavior to attribute tail latency deltas (queue wait vs service time; short vs long class). This PR adds instrumentation in the serving runtime scheduler: (1) trace spans around enqueue/dequeue + classification, (2) per-class queue depth gauges, and (3) wait-time histograms (time from enqueue -> dispatch) for each class and overall. This is designed to support the perf suite + canary A/B jobs without introducing high overhead or high-cardinality metrics.

What’s in this PR (single-string summary): Adds a SchedulerInstrumentation module invoked from the central scheduler hot path; introduces traced spans `runtime.scheduler.enqueue`, `runtime.scheduler.dequeue`, and `runtime.scheduler.dispatch_decision` with minimal attributes; exports stable metric names for dashboards (`runtime_scheduler_queue_depth{class=short|long}`, `runtime_scheduler_wait_time_ms_bucket{class=...}`) with bounded labels; includes an opt-in sampled structured log line for debugging classification/dispatch (off by default); adds a small test shim to validate monotonic wait-time calculations and ensure we don’t emit negative waits under clock skew; updates benchmark runner output parsing to record per-class queue depth and p95 wait-time in the standard summary.

Design notes / constraints: Metrics are intentionally low-cardinality: only `class` (short|long|unknown) + `route_tier` (hosted|dedicated|private) when available; request_id is never a metric label (trace-only). Wait time uses monotonic clock (steady) internally and converts to ms at export. Span attributes are limited to: `class`, `is_streaming`, `tokens_in` (bucketed), `queue_len` (at enqueue), `policy` (fifo|two_queue) (string). All new instrumentation is behind the existing runtime telemetry enablement toggle and respects sampling for traces.

Changed areas (high-level): runtime/scheduler/* (instrumentation hooks), runtime/telemetry/metrics_registry (new metric defs), runtime/telemetry/tracing (new span helpers), runtime/tests/scheduler_instrumentation_test.cc, docs/internal/metrics/runtime_scheduler.md (metric name definitions + units), tools/bench/summary.py (capture and print new fields).

Illustrative snippet (not a full diff): `auto t0 = clock::now(); queues_[cls].push(req); metrics_.queue_depth(cls).Set(queues_[cls].size()); tracer_.Span("runtime.scheduler.enqueue").Attr("class", cls_name).Attr("queue_len", queues_[cls].size()).End(); req->enqueue_time = t0;` and on dequeue: `auto wait_ms = ToMs(clock::now() - req->enqueue_time); metrics_.wait_time_ms(cls).Observe(wait_ms);`.

Testing: Unit tests: SchedulerInstrumentation.WaitTimeNonNegative, SchedulerInstrumentation.QueueDepthTracksEnqueueDequeue. Integration: ran `bench/mixed_workload_replay --scenario short_long_80_20` and verified metrics are emitted + no obvious overhead (CPU +0.6% in local microbench; within noise). No API or config changes.

Follow-ups: Dashboard JSON + alerts in eng-platform repo will be added separately (see ENG-4828). Canary job will consume these metrics once the two-queue policy lands (ENG-4823).

Review conversation (condensed): Allison Grant: Please confirm metric naming/units match standards and histogram buckets are sane. Also avoid `unknown` class unless we truly can’t classify. Author: Aligned names to runtime metrics conventions (snake case, base units in suffix). Buckets: [1,2,5,10,20,50,100,200,500,1000,2000,5000] ms; can be tuned but covers interactive p95/p99. `unknown` only for pre-classifier paths / legacy code paths; it’s still useful to detect instrumentation gaps. Caleb Johnson: Trace attributes include `tokens_in`—is that raw? please bucket to avoid high cardinality + privacy issues. Author: Updated to bucketed `tokens_in_bucket` (<=128, <=512, <=2k, <=8k, >8k) and removed raw token count. Omar El-Sayed: Overhead concerns: tracing in hot loop can be expensive; can we short-circuit when tracer disabled? Author: Added a fast `if (!tracer_.Enabled())` guard and ensured span construction is no-op on disabled builds; metrics remain but use lock-free counters and are already present in runtime. Felix Schneider: For dashboards, we’ll want per-class p95 wait. Ensure histogram has class label and that metric names are stable. Author: Confirmed `class` is a required label; added docs/internal/metrics/runtime_scheduler.md with stability note.

CI status: Buildkite redwood-runtime (pass), unit-tests (pass), clang-tidy (pass), perf-smoke (pass). One initial failure due to missing include for monotonic clock wrapper; fixed in 2nd push.

Merge: Squash merged to main. Release note: none (internal metrics only, but will be referenced by canary runbook).
